record.summary: Informative report by the Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM), considered by the Cabinet of Ministers on 25 February 2025, on putting the EU AI Act into effect in Latvia. It sets out the Act's requirements and what public authorities must do. VARAM is responsible for the Act as a whole; the Ministry of Economics is notifying authority and the Ombudsman the fundamental-rights authority. Twelve market surveillance authorities are named, with the State Data Inspectorate covering prohibited practices and high-risk systems and the Bank of Latvia AI used by financial institutions. It also identifies the legal changes needed and possible additional resources.
record.notes: The report makes the Latvian National Accreditation Bureau the national accreditation body. The twelve market surveillance authorities are the Consumer Rights Protection Centre, the Health Inspectorate, the Civil Aviation Agency, the Latvian Maritime Administration, the State Railway Technical Inspectorate, the State Technical Supervision Agency, the Road Traffic Safety Directorate, the State Service for Quality of Education, the State Data Inspectorate, the State Security Service, the Military Intelligence and Security Service and the Office for Constitutional Protection. The Commission's list of single points of contact for market surveillance under the AI Act (last updated 7 September 2026) names the Consumer Rights Protection Centre for Latvia, without the mark for a pending designation. The Bank of Latvia's supervision was later set out in the Law on Digital Operational Resilience and Use of Artificial Intelligence in Financial Markets (LV-03), and the Artificial Intelligence Centre Law (LV-01) set up the AI Centre.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: re-read VARAM's English press release of 25 February 2025 (stored 12 Oct 2026, unchanged on 17 Oct 2026) and the Commission's page of single points of contact for market surveillance under the AI Act (last updated 7 September 2026). Stored in this run: the same release in Latvian on LV portāls (lvportals.lv, run by the official publisher VSIA 'Latvijas Vēstnesis'), which gives the report's Latvian title. The releases confirm the title, the report's preparation by VARAM, the Cabinet's consideration on 25 February 2025 and the designated authorities; the summary and notes are written from them, not from the report itself, which is not stored (the legal-acts portal TAP, file 24-TA-2633, offers it as a Word file, which textify cannot read). Version 1's statements on PTAC's limited competence (a TAP review seen in search results) and that no general implementing law had been found rested on no stored file and were removed. The references to LV-01 and LV-03 rest on those records' own stored sources.

changes.original_title: copied verbatim from the stored Latvian release, with its typographic quotation marks instead of version 1's single quotes

judgment.status_reasoning: The press release of 25 February 2025 reports that the Cabinet of Ministers considered the report on that day. An informative report taken note of by the Cabinet is a non-binding policy document; no stored file shows it replaced or withdrawn. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A Cabinet-level plan for implementing the EU AI Act nationally, designating the responsible authorities; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: The release is dated 25.02.2025 and says the Cabinet considered the report on Tuesday 25 February. A TAP annotation seen in search results dates the Cabinet's protocol decision 24 February 2025; it is not stored, so the date stays 2025-02-25.
